description: Domain-free cue words of the statement labeller (modules/memory/statements.py, ADR 0036), per language. Every entry is a case-insensitive regular expression matched as whole words; a space matches any run of whitespace. Field meanings: standing - says an instruction outlives the task (always, never, from now on); not_standing - a phrase that contains a standing word but is not one (for good, forever), masked first; obligation and universal - 'All X must ...'; policy_subject - a clause subject that makes 'we never ...' a policy; condition - opens a clause the rule depends on (if, when, whenever); exception - opens the clause a rule does not apply under (unless, except); requester - a word in a condition clause that makes it about the user's own requests or the assistant's work ('when I ask'), so the rule stays a RULE; correction - says something earlier was wrong, at the start of a sentence (correction_start) or anywhere (correction); replacement - the new way replaces an old one (we now use, instead of); lifecycle and status - generic change-of-existence and state words (a domain pack adds its own); status_weak, lifecycle_weak, correction_weak - words that only suggest the kind (closed, new, instead of): the NLI head confirms it with one pair; filler - words that may open an instruction before its verb (please, also, then); only - restricts an instruction to its condition ('only escalate if ...'); addressee - who an instruction acts for (me, us, the manager); generic - an indefinite word that makes a condition any occurrence ('if a delivery is late', 'any change'); consequent - opens the clause after a condition (then, dann, to); subject_start - a word that starts a declarative clause (a pronoun, an article), so a standing word after it describes a habit rather than gives an instruction; imperative - a word that marks an instruction when it opens a clause (please, don't); imperative_inside - one that marks it anywhere in the clause (Hindi mat, Arabic la ta-); imperative_ending - (hi) the ending of an imperative or infinitive-as-imperative verb at the end of a clause, unless it is a declarative_ending; clitic - (ar) what may be written onto the front of a word (wa-, al-, bi-); enclitic - (ar) what may be written onto its end (-ni 'me', the -i of a feminine imperative, the -u of a plural one); request - a verb that opens a one-off request at the start of a sentence; question_start - (en) opens a question even without a question mark, other languages are read by their question marks; auxiliary - (en) a verb that, right after a question word that also opens a condition, makes it a question ('when is', not 'when I ask'); chitchat - greetings, thanks and fillers.
